newsitem.title: UK: Mexico's $1.0 bln FRN seen at LIBOR+140 bp-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's $1.0 bln FRN seen at LIBOR+140 bp-dealers.

text.p: Mexico's $1.0 billion five-year global floating rate note is expected to be priced around 140 basis points over three-month LIBOR, syndicate sources said on Wednesday.
Earlier, bankers said the deal, expected on Thursday, would likely be callable in June 2000.
HSBC and Merrill Lynch are tipped as joint lead managers for the transaction but both declined to comment to the media due to U.S. SEC regulations.
On Tuesday, Mexico said it would prepay a $6.0 billion FRN secured by Pemex oil receivables.

The forthcoming $1.0 billion FRN will go some way towards the refinancing, bankers said. On Tuesday Mexico already raised $500 million via an increase of an existing $1.0 billion bond maturing in January 2007.
"The $6.0 billion prepayment has pumped a lot of cash into the market, and around half of that will be re-invested into emerging market paper," a trader at a U.S. bank said.
"Demand for Mexico's new FRN should be strong as a result," he said.
